_doc: Rules for findings_fold.py, the no-AI findings sorter (FINDINGS_FOLD_BUILD_QUARRY_SAID_IT_23X; design/RimMandrake/findings_curation_design_2026-10-29.md option B, chosen by the owner by card 2026-10-29: "Program folds, FOUNDRY judges"). It runs as the last step of testq-tick.service (testq.py UNITS), after ingest.py. Simplified after two blind reviews (v3_review/blind/findings/review.md, review2.md; coordinator 2026-10-29): the program groups and reports evidence; it never retires, reopens, merges into a decision or writes the ledger.
_out_why: standing.json (the standing-failures table, every raw text kept) and curation.md (FOUNDRY's daily residue) land here: agent scratch, read by FOUNDRY and the Auditor. The one source of this path; FINDINGS_FOLD_OUT overrides it (selftests)
_finding_types_why: the sorter folds what the testq ingest files (type UNTRIAGED, design section 2); hand-filed findings of other types were already judged by the seat that filed them
_lane_item_why: Operations' standing lane item, the one ingest.py already verifies a paused lane against (design section 3, outcome Routed)
_machine_health_patterns_why: routed to Operations, not FOUNDRY: the item says red canaries and machine-health failures go to Operations' lane item; design section 6 names red canaries and refused pulls; a Python module missing on the runner (the PIL fault, design section 2) and a full disk are the test machine's provisioning, not the mod. Case-insensitive regex, searched in the raw text
_contradiction_states_why: design section 6: a failing row under an item marked done or validated is a contradiction and goes to the top of the next curation (the quarry item stood validated with 26 fails and 0 passes). Judged per item: the item's own latest PASS/FAIL of each row its done records map to it (ingest.groups_of)
_decisions_file_why: FOUNDRY's judgment per signature (work / merge / memory / route / retire / undo), appended by `findings_fold.py decide` and committed; a `rimflow spawn --from <finding>` is read from the ledger as a work decision with no line needed
_memory_roots_why: design section 3 and 9.3: memory lands where it is read (a skill, a fact file, a rule or check), never the lessons inbox
_normalise_why: Merge only on an exact signature (coordinator ruling 2026-10-29 after blind review 2): mod + chain + row + the failure text with ONLY these removed, in order: testq job ids (with attempt suffix), compact timestamps (thirst_live_result_<ts>.json keeps its stem), ISO timestamps, durations written as took/elapsed/after/in N s|ms|min, and whitespace runs. Nothing else: hex ids, thing ids, codes, counts and values are KEPT, so two failures that differ in any of them stay two rows. A duplicate row is cheap; a wrong merge loses a bug. Measured over the 2026-10-29 backlog: job ids and compact timestamps were the only volatile tokens
